summary:
We developed a mobile and web-based agricultural decision-support application that leverages NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) data to provide farmers with historical, real-time, and forecasted weather and precipitation analytics. By integrating satellite-derived meteorological data with local soil characteristics, the app calculates effective rainfall—the precise volume of rainwater actually absorbed and retained by the soil rather than lost to runoff or evaporation. This allows farmers to determine exact supplemental irrigation requirements to maintain optimal soil moisture and fertility.

Our solution directly addresses the challenge of water scarcity and erratic rainfall patterns by replacing guesswork with data-driven water management. Instead of relying on raw rainfall totals, which often mislead irrigation schedules, farmers gain actionable insights tailored to their specific field conditions. This is vital for preventing both under-irrigation, which stunts crop yield, and over-irrigation, which leaches soil nutrients, degrades soil health, and wastes diminishing freshwater resources—ultimately supporting long-term agricultural resilience.
details:
Our application acts as an automated agronomic calculator powered by satellite Earth observations to guide post-rainfall irrigation decisions. Farmers begin by inputting their farm’s geographical coordinates alongside basic local soil properties, such as soil texture, infiltration rate, and current crop type, which prompts the app to query the NASA POWER API for localized historical climate trends, surface meteorology, and short-term precipitation forecasts. Because raw rainfall rarely equals usable water for crops, our algorithm processes NASA’s precipitation, temperature, solar irradiance, and humidity datasets to estimate evapotranspiration and surface runoff, calculating the exact effective rainfall absorbed into the root zone. By comparing this figure against the soil's water-holding capacity and crop water demand, the application outputs precise recommendations on whether supplemental irrigation is required and the exact volume needed to maintain soil fertility.

By replacing irrigation guesswork with satellite-backed soil analytics, the platform delivers precision water conservation during droughts while protecting soil health from over-irrigation, nutrient leaching, and erosion. It gives smallholder and resource-limited farmers accessible, enterprise-grade climate adaptation tools without requiring costly on-farm hardware or physical weather stations, ultimately aiming to lower operational expenses, stabilise crop yields amidst erratic weather, and promote sustainable water stewardship. To build and prototype this solution, our team integrated the NASA POWER API with a frontend built using Python (Pandas, NumPy) backend for hydrological modelling, utilising Figma for interface design and VSDC for media and project workflow documentation.

We primarily used AI to generate the source code for our application. We provided AI with prompts based on the application specifications, including inputs, outputs, and calculation methods, which were discussed and decided by our team.

The overall UI layout was designed by our team members. We then used AI to make adjustments and integrate the UI with the calculation functions to complete the application.
